title: kv-cache: adaptive compaction + fragmentation-aware eviction + spillover tuning (v16)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We continue to see tail memory pressure and fragmentation in the KV cache under mixed-length workloads which causes increased paging/spillover and intermittent latency spikes. This PR implements an adaptive compaction path and a fragmentation-aware eviction policy plus spillover tuning to reduce host memory churn and improve p99 latency under realistic customer traces. Summary of changes: 1) Adaptive compaction: background, incremental compaction that runs probabilistically based on fragmentation score and recent allocation churn. 2) Fragmentation-aware eviction: eviction scoring now accounts for fragmented extents and reassembly cost; candidates causing less fragmentation are preferred. 3) Spillover tuning: more conservative paging thresholds and hysteresis to avoid oscillation between RAM and host spill files. 4) Scheduler integration: compaction and eviction tasks are throttled by the serving scheduler and piggyback on idle GPU timeslices to avoid impacting tail latency. 5) Metrics/tracing: added fragmentation_score, compaction_cycles, spillover_hysteresis_state, eviction_reassembly_cost to be emitted per serving node. 6) Tests and benchmarks: new unit tests, integration harness replay against 3 production traces, and a small canary rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-2148) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests (trace replay) - [x] Metrics emitted and dashboards updated - [x] Canary plan and rollout notes prepared Rollout and safety: This is feature-gated and off by default. We will enable in a small set of Dedicated hosts for 72h, monitor fragmentation_score and p99 latency, then expand. If memory spill increases or p99 regresses, the gate will be rolled back. Why this approach: previous heuristics were too aggressive on compaction and caused unnecessary CPU cycles and scheduling interference; the new approach is incremental and scheduler-aware which keeps GC-like work off the critical path. Benchmarks: Seen improvements on three representative traces: - trace-a (consumer-chat): p99 generation latency down 12% (1.8s -> 1.58s), average host memory used down 18% - trace-b (long-context assist): reduced spillover file reads by 42% and stable p95 - trace-c (burst load): tail latency improvements of 9% and 33% fewer OOM-equivalent spill events Testing notes: unit tests cover compaction heuristics, eviction scoring, and spillover hysteresis. Integration replay validated behavior on mixed-sequence workloads and confirmed no increase in amplified GC CPU. CI: flaky tests fixed; one lint failure caused by formatting was addressed. See commits for details.
